interactions.title: Hulda’s commission and the elven archivist
lines: DM: Despite the misgivings of various party members, you meet… met Lord Hulda, who was… what, proud, bitter? Resentful? Over the hill? Not in a cliched sort of way, but with the sense of the best days being behind already, and it wasn't that great anyways. Stuck on a wheel, always turning, one year after the next, always different, but always the same.

DM: He tells you the story of this elven archivist, who… self, who called himself an archivist, who gave him a deed to the house, to its… the house, its lands, and all the treasures therein, on the condition that Hulda asked you to step through a door in the floor and convince a man beyond to end a long-held treaty.

before: Edric: Now we got it.
DM: Great. Alright. Ready? Yeah. Yeah.

DM: The five of you who have been adventuring and traveling together for the better part of this last year, have been hired by a minor lord named Hulda, the second son of a no-name lord from southern Sembara, who spent the last 25 years or more as an adventurer and sellsword, always trying to find and make his fortune, and never quite succeeding in it. Last spring, after killing a dragon that had come down from the north, and losing his entire party in the process, and discovering… since it was a wandering dragon, there was no hoard, that he had nothing more in his purse than he did 3 decades ago when he left home. He was drinking his misery away when a long-lived elf approached him and gave him the deed to a… house in the wilderness, in the far north of Sembara, or northwest of Tollen, in a place that was long, long since swallowed by woods.

DM: You were hired by Alden, a small, stout, pale human, with a curiosity about you all, and a profound fear of fire, apparently, to go there. As you journey there over the course of several days, first going upriver and then crossing through the forest, which got denser, older, wilder, and less inhabited the further you went into it. You at last came to Dandelion House, a marvel of late Drankorian architecture, at least 700 years old, and the funny combination of both glorious and decrepit.

DM: Parts of it… The windows and the wooden window frames were decayed away into powder, as was much of the furniture inside, but not all of it. There must be some sort of preservation magic woven through the structure.
after: DM: Hulda, whose only negotiation strategy, in fact, maybe his only strategy for moving through the world, period, seems to be intimidation, failed immediately to convince the man on the other side of this door of anything, and turned to the party for help. Tarek, reading the document, knew that something didn't fit, but Kaito, by this point, had gone from deep fear bordering on paranoia to excitement bordering on rapturous enthusiasm. Correct. And, the… Ayveen, correct me if I'm saying any of the names wrong. Ayveen, observes that ending an unknown treaty may not, in fact, be a wise course of action to take, and Txarro points out that the treasure could equally well be a trap or metaphor. Nonetheless…

DM: The party arises before dawn, woken by the grandfather clock, still in fine condition. And Alden collects you from your rooms, leads you down through the ground floor, down through a massive basement, and down further still, opening a locked door with a glowing gold key, down through a passage hewn from living rock into a root-covered subcellar that surely predates the entire manor above it, and in fact, on reflection, subcellar isn't even quite the right thing, you… assumed at the moment that's probably what it was, given its position below the cellar. But there was nothing in it but these walls covered entirely in massive, hollowed-out, massive roots, rather.

DM: Hulda is waiting there, and opens a door through this massive hollowed-out root, promising to keep an eye on this end while you go through and take care of business on the far. Once you get to the far side, he says, go up and up, and out and onto the road, and you'll see the manor just a little ways ahead, and seek there the master of the house.

DM: Just as he closes the door behind you, Tarek realizes the unsettling thing about the contract is that it was 400 years old, but written in contemporary Sembaran. Considering, setting up… sort of a note of… confusion.

DM: We open in this moment, illuminated by a couple of light spells, I think, as the five of you are crawling single file through this tunnel, barely bigger, barely bigger than you, making your way towards who knows what.

DM: If he hears your message, he makes no response. But I don't think there's a way to know if the spell failed. Yeah. Hmm.

interactions.title: Edric trusts the Night Queen in the strange realm
lines: Edric: ((Appearance and verbal scaffolding)) the Night Queen will watch over these strange places, will watch over me in these strange places. ((Film comparison)) the Night Queen… the Night Queen watches our sleep, this is… this is… We are not on the other side, this is not the land of the dead. Will be safe. It'll all turn out. Kind of in a… like in a mantra kind of vibe.
Edric: 100% absolute confidence, but every once in a while, he's, like, falters a little bit and kind of looks around at, like, everybody, like: “Is this really gonna work out?”

before: Kaito Min: Hair's kind of blowing all crazy in the wind, and he, like, opens up his, his, robe. He's always got this, like, you know, really… On a very beautiful, flowing red robe with gold— some gold patterning. Just kind of lets it all fly out. Like, put his, put his arm… Like, kind of pulls off his, like, pack and, like, his instruments and stuff, they all, like, tumble together… ground. It just, like, is like this: Ugh… And then he, like, pauses, and he's like… “Guys… We're in one now.”
Kaito Min: And in his mind, he's like… He's like… “Gotta not be so all over the place, Kaito. Get your shit together, dude. Get your shit together. You can do this. You can do this.”

Tarek: Tarek is next to him, looking over, like… “Get your shit together, man.” And he is… exerting his, you know, 20-something streetwise confidence while… internally panicking a little bit as he looks around. He's, Tarek has… he's like, thrift store deluxe looking. He's got the… very high-end threads that are very beat up.
DM: Store Deluxe, we love it.

Edric: Edric is… clutching his, you know, he has this… big two-handed maul that he carries around, right, for, like, hitting things with. He's kind of holding it a little… more tightly than normal, and… his… he has, like, his breastplate, like, he… he sort of has one hand, like, on the holy symbol of the Night Queen on his breastplate, like, kind of holding it for comfort, another hand kind of… grasped around his weapon. It's probably still, like, slung over his back, it's probably… well, no, it's probably… he probably drew it, right? Like, he's in a weird spot. He's probably drawn his maul.
after: Kaito Min: Nice.

Txarro: So, Txarro has drawn himself up to his full… 6'4"… lizardfolk height. Slung his wooden shield off of his back and is holding it in front of him. His, like… cloak kind of tossed back his, greenish-yellow scales on his head. He's quivering slightly as his, like, nostrils are flaring, and he's… trying to be deeply attuned to whatever might be happening.

Txarro: And… kind of looking around at Kaito, and Tarek, and Edric, and… Ayveen's maybe less nervous than the rest of them, but… You know, he feels a little… you know, he's a… he's not old, but he's, like, a decade older than, well, everybody except Kaito, obviously. But Kaito's sitting here saying, “Get your shit together, get your shit together.” Give off the appearance of an elder.
Kaito Min: No.

Txarro: And you can, you can see, like, if you look at him closely, you see there's, like, every now and then, there's, like, little… you can almost see, like, little streaks of, like, tiger fur growing on his scales as if he's… poised at the ready to turn into a tiger, should the need call for it. But for the moment, striding confidently ahead, trying to… see what's here, and what mysteries this place might bring. Let's follow the path, I guess.

interactions.title: The murdered traveler appears to have been a wizard
lines: DM: Yeah, they have 3 long… green-feathered arrows protruding from their back. And their head has been completely… smashed into nothingness. Like, after they died, someone stood there, flattening it systematically. It's human-sized, it is extremely difficult to tell from what remains of it.

DM: With the 20, with a 20, it's clear that… this person was in motion when they were struck from behind with the arrows. So they're… they're splayed out, you get the impression that they were probably running, away from something and shot from behind.
DM: Oh, sorry, a human, yeah.
Tarek: Which direction? The direction we're walking?
DM: Sorry, like, mid-20s, something like that, relatively young.
Txarro: And they were running… back towards the… Coral House, or…
Kaito Min: Running away from the…
DM: Nope, towards… towards the direction you came from.

DM: Also in the pockets, there's a… belt knife… And there are, a whole series of little pouches and pockets filled with… anything and everything that you recognize as spell components. Bits of copper wire, and the skull of a mouse, and… cotton fluff, and… on and on. Nothing that's worth anything on its own, but enough to make you think this was probably a wizard.

before: DM: Yeah.

DM: And as you get a little closer, sure, yeah, everyone can see it as you pass.
Txarro: I mean, I'll… I'll point it out.
Edric: Is it… I'll walk over, I mean, is it? Is this person dead?

interactions.title: A prayer for the way out
lines: Kaito Min: Kaito goes over to Edric and, like, gives him, like, from behind, and is like, “You know, Edric, however long we've been hanging out, you always talk about… the night… what is it, the night?”
Kaito Min: You're always talking on and on about the Night Queen. I gotta say, I'm with you now. Do your Night Queen shit? Like, what's the… what's that?

Kaito Min: Is the Night Queen, like, helping us? Like, I am… I am… This is the… maybe the only time you'll ever see me do this, but let's… let's say a prayer together. What are we saying? Like, what do we…
Edric: We'll send a prayer to her, asking her to ask the Wanderer to show us the path out.

Kaito Min: “Wanderer, show us the…” like, Kaito gets on his knees, like, pray, like… deep authenticity, like, “Wanderer, show us the path out,” and kind of, like, glances over at the body, and he's like… Never believed in the Night Queen so hard right now. Let's go.

before: Kaito Min: Like, what's your…
Tarek: Almost?
Edric: Edric?

after: DM: About a half mile…
Edric: It'll be…

DM: From the manor, a line, a hedgerow, tall, maybe 15 feet and solid, sort of like a wall itself, comes up the hill, from the… river that's… flowing by, down, away from you. And you find yourselves following this wall along the side of the road, this high hedge, until at last ahead, maybe a few hundred feet… Excellent.

Txarro: Before we get… Before we get super close to the manor, we saw… When we were seeing it from a distance, we saw, like, lights around it, and it looked like… I mean, do we still see there's, like… people? Or…

You hear… improbably what sounds like it might be a string quartet, or some combination of… string players in the distance. And a murmur of sounds from outside the house and grounds.

interactions.title: The roadkeepers warn of the bad smell
lines: DM: The guards raise a hand in greeting. But then a look of confusion comes over their face. They're two deeply, deeply wrinkled, sort of elderly men. Pot-bellied… with, you know, the sort of hoods that someone wears that's just, like, the separate hood from the cloak. And they… they look at you with a note of confusion, and then…

DM: And then lift their noses to sniff, and sniff almost dog-like, and in their sniffing, there's a strange moment of not understanding if you're seeing men pretending to be dogs, or dogs pretending to be men. But they finished that, and then nod a greeting, and say, “Well met and welcome, mortals.”
Kaito Min: Kaito gives a flourish. “Greetings.” But before he walks in, though, he's, he glances and says, “The festivities ending soon?”
DM: Indeed. Indeed. The party is ending. You're just in time.
DM: “The party before it ends,” says one, with a chuckle. Indeed. My favorite time. Yeah, he gets ahold of that.
DM: Where have you… come from? It's unusual to see so many of you together at once at this time of night. Damn.
Kaito Min: Where did we come from? Down the road, of course.
DM: The one who hasn't said anything so far chuckles, like you've made a very incisive joke.
Kaito Min: And may I ask, can you share more about the party? Well, our apologies for being late.
DM: I'll tell you this: We belong to the road… to the party… The party isn't our story. We know what we hear and smell and see through the gate, but this is as far as we go.
Kaito Min: Well… Perhaps some candor. We came from the road. We saw bodies. Presumably coming from here.
Kaito Min: I love a good party. Gives another flourish and a wink. But also, the bodies. Anything you might be able to share about the party and the Lord here?
DM: The ones you passed did not come from this house, but further up the road.
DM: In the Twilight Kingdom, there are a dozen dozen houses, homes, and holes, with the setting sun just over the horizon.
Kaito Min: This is the Twilight Kingdom.
Edric: Which… Which way is the road going? Towards the sun? Away from…

DM: The road goes almost, as near as you can tell, the road goes parallel… to what in any other place would be the north-south axis, exactly between day and night. And you notice, in fact, having been here for at least an hour now, that the sun has not moved in the sky.
DM: Do you have… Sensing your confusion, the same guard says, “Do you have, where you’re from, disease that spreads from one… person to another?”

DM: Well, we don't have that here. But we have something… similar, something, mmm… Sometimes people get infected in a way… Sometimes people get caught by a bad smell. And that smell… can cause disaster and spread to more people with the bad smell.
DM: We belong to the road. We keep the road safe. Sometimes, the people with the bad smell you can't get the bad smell out of them any other way. I think that's what you saw.
Kaito Min: So… The bodies… you guys don't have anything to do with the bodies?
DM: My people do, some of us stay at the gate, some of us travel the road.
Kaito Min: But you don't know what to do with the bodies?
DM: The two of us? No. No, no. Our place is the gate.
Kaito Min: Right. And, and again, the Lord of the manor here? What do you know of him?

DM: He came to the gate once. He came to the gate once. Just at the height of the party, just before… You know what it's like? When a gathering starts to come apart, you can feel it before anyone's even left. He came in that moment, to tell us to… be careful, careful of travelers on the road, to smell very carefully for the bad smell, but to let in any mortal who wanted entrance.
DM: It was a strange thing, I remember it, too. I would have thought he just said “any guest who wanted entrance”, but he said “any mortal who wants entrance, send them in.”
Kaito Min: When was this directive?
DM: Just, just, just as the party began to end. Just after the height of it. We arrived, of course, when it was just beginning.
Kaito Min: Oh, so very… quite recently. How long has this party been going?
DM: He shakes his head, confused, like you're asking a sort of a ridiculous question. Began and reached its peak, and now it's coming apart.
Kaito Min: Well, you just said the bodies, they're not from here, they're not from this house, the bodies are from another house. Do you know what house they're from?
DM: There's a house… that when people come out of, they come out of it with the bad smell sometimes. What?
Edric: What does that smell like?
Edric: So we can avoid it.

DM: He looks thoughtful and deep for a sec, and then locks in eye contact with you and says: “It smells exactly unlike anything else I have ever smelled in my entire living. It’s the opposite of smell.”
Txarro: Are there other mortals with this party?
DM: There's a handful, a few have come by boat. The halflings came soon after it began. They always seem to. Thanks.
DM: I think there was a dwarf… he turns to the other one, the dwarf went in, did they come out? And a few I couldn't quite tell. None of them had the bad smell, though.
DM: Would you like to go in?
Edric: The house down at the end of the road, the one that's kind of fallen apart?
DM: He says in a language you don't recognize what surely must be some curse and spits. It's a bad-smelling place. We don't go there.
Txarro: Does the road end in the other direction, too?
DM: Roads don't end. They only ever go… on and on.
Edric: No, some roads don't… Edric, like, covers up his mouth, like, I probably shouldn’t get in an argument with them and stop talking.
DM: “We belong to the road,” he says. “We know.”

before: Kaito Min: And the goal here, though, is, yeah, we don't say anything out loud about what we're here for yet, but… You know, let's just, let's just feel it out and see. You know, don't think there's anything here that's gonna kill us right away. What do you guys think?
Txarro: The owl overhead.
DM: As you're coming up to the gate, the last thing that you see through the owl's eyes, just before the guards notice you, and sort of stand and… rub their eyes and raise a hand to hail you.
DM: In one of the doors of the manor, illuminated brightly from behind, a tall… man? Stands, stepping… with a sort of a lithe grace like a dancer into the doorway.

DM: With the backlighting, it's difficult to tell… if the… smoothness of his face is his face itself, or like a sort of a mask, like a masquerade kind of mask that he's been… put… on. But you… you see him scan over the crowd. You see his eyes fall away down the slope of the hills, to where the… people are climbing into the rowboat to head onwards. You see him note sharp voices raised among a small, cluster of people off and away below the, below the patios. And then you see him look directly at the owl and make eye contact, nod to himself, and step back inside the house.
after: Txarro: Should we go in? Txarro says to everybody else, in… Tollish, not Common. Which I presume everybody understands.
Kaito Min: Let's do it.
Txarro: We would like to enter.
DM: Very good. Did you bring gifts?

Kaito Min: You know, I literally was gonna say that at the very beginning, that, unfortunately… Well, I'll put it this way: We may have… gifts are a relative term. In the sense that, something that I possess may be a gift to some, it may not be to others. So, we come bearing our possessions. To the extent that some of those may be worthy and deemed gifts, then we have them.

review.reason: The two guards are distinguishable, but the narration does not assign every reply to an individual; the principal exchange is retained without relabeling DM speech.

interactions.title: The gatekeeper accepts dreams as an entry gift
lines: Txarro: Should we go in? Txarro says to everybody else, in… Tollish, not Common. Which I presume everybody understands.
Txarro: We would like to enter.
DM: Very good. Did you bring gifts?
Txarro: Would he approve of me sharing my gifts with you?
DM: Listen. I am bribable. Tell me this instead, and I'll let you through. It's been so long since I've gotten to speak with anyone who dreams. What did you dream of last time you slept? Wow.
Txarro: Most of my dreams are of animals, which you seem to have few of here.
Txarro: Have you… heard of… I'm just trying to think of an interesting bird, that would live in some… in Tollen.
DM: Shouldn't be gone. No, what do they smell like?
Txarro: And of mud and reeds.

Txarro: I dreamt of one, wandering, lost, through a marsh, calling its low, hooting noise, trying to find… What? I don't know. But as it reached the… edge of the reed bed came out of the water onto the mud. It began to… carry and dig. And as it did, it turned into… a snake, and slithered through the dirt, shedding its skin as it went, which grew into reeds, until it came to the water again, and sprouted feathers from its now bare skin growing into a bittern again, calling a low, moaning noise.
DM: Was the bird at the end the same or different from the bird at the beginning?
DM: Very good. And he's not satisfied.

DM: Or are you satisfied? That, I… listen, I, I, I don't… I don't mean to be greedy. But it's a precious opportunity, wouldn't you agree? I've always wondered what it's like, what do you make of these things? Ed?
Edric: Edric says: “I… I normally dream of… baking bread? Just the smell of it.”
DM: Mmm, I know that smell. That's a good smell.
Edric: But… then sometimes there's the other dream. But maybe I shouldn't speak of it here.
DM: It's a little… He kind of rumbles. Hmm… I'm curious now, though, what is this other… other dream? You make it sound like it's unchosen. You don't get to choose your dreams?
Edric: No, no. But dreams come from the gods. You don't know that?
DM: I don't dream. I only smell.
Edric: Well… There's the one… where I'm lying in a grave.
DM: Oof, not enough. What's the…

Edric: And then… a crown appears. 6 points of light, coming through the dirt? And I'm small, I can't… move my… on my own very well, I can only crawl. And the crown gets brighter and brighter, and I know to follow it. I think it might be a memory, in a way?
Kaito Min: It might be a what?
Edric: A memory, in a way.
Edric: And then the grave dissolves. Then I wake up.
DM: When you're in the grave, is it open to the sky, or are you under dirt?
Edric: No, it's… it's dirt until the… until the light starts to… the six points of light start to melt it away. Almost like, like a beam, like…

Edric: He waves… Edric sort of waves his hand, and then… and ball of light appeared, like a… but wait this… And he closes his fist, and it goes away again. But 6 of them, like a crown, tunneling their way through.
DM: Guard nods: “Grave smell is a good smell. Like a bath, it cleans. It's good that you're in the grave, sometimes.”
Edric: Have you never smelled a bad grave smell?
DM: Once I smelled the bad smell for the first time, nothing else was bad anymore, except for it.
Kaito Min: Sorry, where's the bad smell come from again?
DM: Bad smell comes from… the mortals who catch it.
Kaito Min: Are any of the mortals who here have it?
DM: No, no one… no one inside these grounds does. That's what we're here for: to sniff it out, to keep it from entry.
DM: One more dream, and I'll let you through.

Kaito Min: Yeah, I'll tell you, I'll tell you a dream. But before I do… onto gifts, Kaito pulls out his lute, and what is the other instrument that he has? He's… he has… He pulls out… oh no. How do I not have my…

Kaito Min: Anyways, he pulls out, he pulls out a, like, a stringed instrument and a, like, a small flute. And, he just… he gives, like, both of them just, like, a quick little flourish, but, like, of incredible skill. It's just, like, “Oh, this guy can definitely play these things.” But not too showy, but just, like, a little… just to, like, to show.
Kaito Min: And, he, he says: “Does the Lord of the Manor appreciate skill in song, in music? Presumed so. As gifts, anyway.”
DM: I don't… I don't know. It's a good offer to make.
Kaito Min: Dreams. You know, I find my dreams, it's never one thing. The dreams are always one thing connected into another thing, into another.
Kaito Min: Can I share one of those? Yeah. Yeah.

Kaito Min: Well, you know, my kinds, we actually have one dream. And it only happens once, so… I actually share your nostalgia. Well, I guess you're… for you, it's a curiosity, since you've never had a dream, right? Isn't that correct?
Kaito Min: Yeah, I, I, I empathize with that, but for me, it's more nostalgia, because I've only ever had one dream. But if you like, I can share you some snippets of that dream.

Kaito Min: Well… Well, it was the one dream, and it was a long dream. There were parts of the dream, the parts that I'm nostalgic for the most. It's less one moment or one narrative and more just a whole bunch of scenes clipped and chopped and strewn together, almost like a patchwork of a quilt that, you know, is made of so many different colors and shapes and textures and smells.

Kaito Min: But it would go from… one scene with just massive trees of unimaginable size, swaying in huge roots and just… large, craggy grass, and this kind of feeling of something so raw and alive. And then all of a sudden, nothingness in the night sky, and just… black. Except stars. Everywhere. And then shifting from stars to blackness.

Kaito Min: And then all of a sudden, the crashing of waves smashing over your head, and you're in a boat rocking up and down, and up and down, and your body's swaying back and forth, and then you feel like you're in the middle of the ocean, except you're not. You're in the middle of a fire, and you're in a flame inside of the fireplace, and it's just raging hot, and you're sweating, and it's just so incredibly uncomfortable, until you hear the sound of a voice singing.

hanging lanterns welcome you. A party begins. Lord Revel Beginning.”

hanging lanterns flicker low. A party ending. Lord Endless Ending.”
